articles.title: Andy Burnham signals he may lift ban on alcohol in football stands
articles.summary: Prime minister says measure is discriminatory when fans of other sports are not similarly restricted. Andy Burnham has signalled he may lift the ban on drinking alcohol in the stands at football matches, suggesting it is “unfair” for fans to be singled out when it is permitted for other sports.
body: The prime minister, a committed Everton fan who still attends matches, said there was a case for trialling an end to the ban to bring football in line with rugby and cricket.

The move was welcomed by the Football Supporters’ Association and the English Football League, but police warned it would be “incredibly rash” to make changes without considering their impact on safety.
Burnham has long opposed the ban, saying it is discriminatory and out of date, harking back to an era when football violence was fuelled by drinking within view of the pitch.

Asked by reporters on the plane to New York about lifting a ban, Burnham said: “I don’t think it’s fair for football fans to be singled out in that way and I made that point. I think that legislation dates to an era where football was very different. And I do believe there is a case to remove that discrimination.

articles.title: Christian Eriksen leaves Wolfsburg by mutual consent after on-pitch collapse in June
articles.summary: Danish midfielder has been recuperating in homeland. Eriksen: ‘I’m pleased we were able to find a solution’ Christian Eriksen and the German side VfL Wolfsburg have agreed to terminate ⁠his contract by mutual consent, the club announced on Wednesday.
body: The 34-year-old collapsed during a Denmark friendly ⁠against Ukraine in June. Eriksen said in July he would ​return to his homeland to undergo a ‌rehabilitation programme. He previously suffered a cardiac arrest during Denmark’s opening Euro 2020 group match ⁠against Finland in Copenhagen in 2021.

The decision brings ⁠an early end ⁠to ​Eriksen’s contract, which was set to run until June 2027. The midfielder joined Wolfsburg as a free agent a year ago, making 34 appearances across all competitions. Eriksen scored three goals and provided 10 assists for the Wolves, but could not prevent their relegation from the Bundesliga.

“At the moment, it is important for me to ‌be close to my family in Denmark. I’m pleased that we were able to find a solution together,” Eriksen said in a statement. “My time in Wolfsburg was marked by many highs and lows,” he added. “I know that the club is now ‌in good hands as it aims to make its way back to the Bundesliga, and I am convinced ​that a successful future lies ahead for VfL.”

articles.title: Former NFL star Antonio Brown to avoid possibility of 30 years in prison with plea deal
articles.summary: 38-year-old had been facing attempted murder charge. Former player will accept aggravated assault charge. Former NFL star Antonio Brown plans to accept a plea deal on an attempted murder charge in Miami, his lawyer said Wednesday. Doing so will mean the former wide receiver avoids prison.
body: Brown is scheduled to appear in court next Wednesday to make the deal final. He could face up to 30 years in prison if convicted of the current attempted murder charge.

“They made [Brown] an offer he couldn’t refuse,” Brown’s attorney, Mark Eiglarsh, said in a statement. “There is a profound difference between believing you can win a case and deciding that you and your family cannot afford to spend another year, or potentially several years, wearing an ankle monitor and fighting it.”

Brown is accused of grabbing a handgun from a member of security after a celebrity boxing match in Miami in May 2025. The 38-year-old is then alleged to have fired two shots at a man he had gotten into a fistfight with earlier, according to an arrest warrant. Zul-Qarnain Kwame Nantambu told investigators that one of the bullets grazed his neck.
Nantaumbu’s attorney, Richard L Cooper, said this month that his client has forgiven Brown and would no longer take part in the case against the former player.

Doing so will mean the former wide receiver avoids prison.

articles.title: Harry Kane admits England’s World Cup 2026 exit ‘hurt more than any other’
articles.summary: ‘It wasn’t the team that we wanted and said we’d be’ England host Spain in Nations League on Saturday. Harry Kane has described England’s World Cup semi-final defeat against Argentina as his most painful tournament exit because of how the team lost sight of who they were.
body: The captain is determined to move on as quickly as possible and is chasing a statement performance against Spain at Wembley on Saturday night in the Nations League. But he admits he is yet to get over the Argentina game and knows it is something he and his England teammates must work to process.

“It felt like it wasn’t us as a team,” Kane said, as he reflected on how England lost their way in the 2-1 defeat, barely touching the ball after they went ahead in the 55th minute. “It wasn’t the team that we wanted to be and said we’d be. When you maybe go against your beliefs and you lose, it feels 10 times worse than just losing in a way where … if we lose doing it our way you accept it, take it on the chin and move on. It’s tough and it will still be tough.

“I’m so passionate about England and especially because I’ve been on this journey … been to finals, semi‑finals and been so close. Each one hurts in a different way and this one hurt, for sure, more than any other one. I’d say even more than when I missed the penalty in Qatar [in the 2-1 defeat by France in the 2022 World Cup quarter-finals] because of just the manner that it happened.”

articles.title: When Bellamy watched on as Ronaldo caused lockdown
articles.summary: Craig Bellamy says Cristiano Ronaldo is "beyond a superstar" before his Wales side face the Portugal legend in the opening match of their Nations League A campaign.
body: With five Ballon d'Or wins, eight league titles, five Champions Leagues, a European Championship and a pair of Nations League triumphs among his glut of honours, Cristiano Ronaldo's status as one of football's all-time greats is not in doubt.
But a chance encounter with the Portugal legend helped Wales boss Craig Bellamy appreciate that the 41-year-old is significantly more than just a footballing icon.
Bellamy was on a pre-season trip to Lisbon during his time as an assistant to manager Vincent Kompany at Burnley when the Portuguese capital's airport was effectively put into lockdown.
It led to the Welshman describing Ronaldo as "beyond a superstar" after he realised the vast presence of police and security officials were to help escort the global icon.

articles.title: Aaron Glenn Reveals the Dan Campbell Promise He Still Remembers
articles.summary: Aaron Glenn’s return to Ford Field this Sunday will be a competitive one. It will also carry the weight of a friendship that began long before he became the New York Jets’ head coach.
body: Glenn spent four seasons as Dan Campbell’s defensive coordinator in Detroit, helping build a culture that moved the Lions from an NFL afterthought to a division champion and NFC contender. Ahead of his first head-to-head meeting with Campbell as a head coach, Glenn reflected on the promise his longtime friend made to him years ago.
“Dan had told me a long time ago, ‘Whenever I get a head coaching job, I want you to be my coordinator,’” Glenn said in a Jets team feature. “That friendship will always last.”

That promise became reality when Campbell hired Glenn as his defensive coordinator in 2021. Four years later, Glenn returns to Detroit leading the Jets, while Campbell prepares to face one of the coaches who helped define the early years of his Lions tenure.

Glenn’s rise from defensive coordinator to NFL head coach did not happen by accident. Campbell trusted him with major responsibilities in Detroit and treated him as more than a position coach elevated to a new title.

articles.title: Autumn wheeze: Brewers 4, Phillies 1
articles.summary: The offense was already in post-season form as the Philadelphia Phillies (87-71) were stifled by the Milwaukee Brewers (99-59) on Wednesday night in the middle stanza of their penultimate series of the regular season.
body: Aaron Nola was responsible for all four of the Brewers’ runs, surrendering solo home runs to Brice Turang and Christian Yelich in the first and second innings and a two-run single to William Contreras in the third.
The Phillies loaded the bases with no outs against Brewers’ starter, Logan Henderson, in the bottom of the second but came away with just one run on a ground out by JT Realmuto.
11 Phillies reached base on six hits, four walks and a hit-by-pitch against Kyle Schwarber but were 0-12 with runners in scoring position, their worst mark of the season.
Though he accounted for the lone RBI, Realmuto is mired in the worst hitless streak of his career, which reached 26 at-bats.

articles.title: Young Infielder’s Transformation Makes Him Essential Hitter for White Sox
articles.summary: No one predicted that Chicago White Sox infielder Chase Meidroth would launch 16 home runs, put up a four-win season, and be a top-30 position player before the 2026 season began.
body: ‎Meidroth has become one of the trusted players on manager Will Venable ‘s roster since August, and the timing of his development is crucial to the team. On Tuesday, he went 3-for-4 with a three-run homer, a two-run single, and five RBI as the White Sox earned a 14-11 win over the Kansas City Royals in their first game of the three-game set this week. In a tight American League Central race with the Cleveland Guardians, Meidroth could be the most important offensive player for the White Sox.

After hitting five home runs in 2025, Chase Meidroth entered spring training for the 2026 season with the intention of adjusting his swing mechanics to contact the ball earlier in front of the home plate. That drastic decision more than doubled his ISO from.067 to.138, while his overall offensive rating rose from an 87 wRC+ in 2025 to 112 in 2026. With that, there has been a decline in his physical bat speed from 67.4 mph in 2025 to 66.9 mph in 2026.

articles.title: Itauma 'humiliated' but may never lose again - Hrgovic
articles.summary: Moses Itauma may never lose again if he can get over the "humiliation" of his IBF heavyweight title defeat, says Filip Hrgovic, who stunned the Briton in August.
body: The Croatian, 34, stopped Itauma, who had been the strong pre-fight favourite, in the ninth round of their meeting at the O2 Arena.
The early signs suggested Itauma had the measure of his opponent, with Hrgovic touching the canvas in the second round and conceding that he was "outboxed" early on.
Hrgovic took advantage when Itauma tired but stressed the 21-year-old southpaw is so skilful that he could go on to have a hugely succesful career if he learns from his loss.
"He's really good. He's special. Very fast, very talented and he countered whatever I tried with his speed and timing," said Hrgovic.

articles.title: Kaptein scores winner as Chelsea earn narrow victory over Austria Wien
articles.summary: Wieke Kaptein scored a stunning goal but Chelsea were given a stern test by Austria Wien as they began their Women's Champions League campaign with a hard-fought 1-0 win at Plough Lane.
body: Chelsea went ahead in spectacular style early on. Sandy Baltimore's run was ended by a well-timed sliding tackle and the ball spun loose. Collecting it 25 yards from goal was Kaptein, and after taking a touch she hammered it in off the bar.
Keira Walsh was forced off injured after 20 minutes, a potential blow for Chelsea ahead of Sunday's WSL game at home to Arsenal.

The home side were living dangerously when goalkeeper Livia Peng fumbled a shot from a short corner routine, palming the ball back out into danger from where Virginia Kirchberger hoisted it over the bar.
There was almost a sublime equaliser when Louise Schoffel danced her way through Chelsea's defence and hit a low shot that flashed inches wide of the post.

articles.title: Does Littler need to change approach to hostile crowds?
articles.summary: Following Luke Littler's latest run-in with a hostile crowd over the weekend, the Sky Sports Love The Darts Podcast has debated whether it is time for the world champion to change his approach.
body: Littler's bid for a clean sweep of all major PDC titles in 2026 was ended on Sunday after a crushing 10-4 defeat to Jonny Clayton in the last eight at the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam, but the action was overshadowed by the Brit's unhappiness at being repeatedly whistled at by the Dutch crowd.

After facing significant hostility during his win over home favourite Danny Noppert on Friday, Littler threatened to boycott future tournaments in the Netherlands after being booed and whistled at during his victory over Nathan Aspinall on Saturday, prompting referee Charlie Corstorphine to intervene.
Littler has taken a stance against volatile crowds before, refusing to travel to European Tour events in Germany as a result of his treatment from fans there.

On the latest episode of the Love The Darts Podcast, World Series of Darts Finals champion Ross Smith explained his own approach to hostile crowds, which he admits is inspired by three-time world champion Michael van Gerwen.

articles.title: Fantasy football Week 3 Start 'Em & Sit 'Em: Chuba Hubbard continues heater with a top-10 finish in sight
articles.summary: Jamey Eisenberg cautions Fantasy managers not to overreact after the first two weeks, but highlights several players with new opportunities to produce big due to a rash of injuries
body: The theme for Week 3 -- and maybe the season -- is surviving injuries. It's been a rough start so far with players getting hurt.
At quarterback, we just lost Jaxson Dart (knee) for the season, and Jayden Daniels (elbow) and Caleb Williams (hamstring) could miss several weeks. That's a lot of star power out for that position.

Running back has a lengthy list of injuries that we need to monitor, including Saquon Barkley (shoulder), Jadarian Price (shoulder), Travis Etienne (hamstring), Aaron Jones (knee), Rico Dowdle (toe) and all three Broncos running backs. J.K. Dobbins (hip), RJ Harvey (hamstring), and Jonah Coleman (ankle) are all hurt heading into Week 3 against the Rams, and whoever is the healthiest might be a must-start Fantasy running back.

At wide receiver, we're keeping an eye on Puka Nacua (groin), Malik Nabers (shoulder), Mike Evans (hip), Nico Collins (hamstring), D.J. Moore (shoulder) and Zay Flowers (hamstring), among others. With A.J. Brown (ankle) on injured reserve, this position has taken a beating so far this season with several players who were selected in the early part of the draft.
